findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_booking_request" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_availability, get_property_details, get_policies · Private data: get_policies · Public sink: get_property_details, get_policies, create_booking_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_availability, get_property_details, get_policies · Private data: get_policies · Public sink: get_property_details, get_policies, create_booking_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_availability" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
